chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Mihran ibn Muhammad from Sa'd ibn Zarif from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'As for he who gives and fears God and certifies the best [reward]'
He said: 'Indeed Allah gives for one tenfold to a hundred thousand and more'
'Then We will ease him toward ease'
He said: 'He does not desire any good except that Allah makes it easy for him'
'And as for he who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient'
He said: 'He is stingy with what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, gave him'
'Indeed Allah the Exalted gives for one tenfold to a hundred thousand and more'
'Then We will ease him toward hardship'
He said: 'He does not desire any evil except that it is made easy for him'
'And his wealth will not avail him if he falls'
He said: 'By Allah, it is not a fall into a well, nor from a mountain, nor from a wall, but a fall into the fire of Hell.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic term 'taradda' (falling) refer to in the context of stinginess according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the verses of Surah Al-Shams by defining 'Al-Husna' (the Good) as the ultimate reward of Paradise and 'Al-Usla' (the Evil) as the ease of Hellfire for the stingy. It specifically clarifies that the 'falling' (taradda) of the miser is not a physical descent but a spiritual plunge into the Fire, emphasizing that material wealth becomes utterly useless in that state. This interpretation is central to Shia exegesis of Surah Al-Shams, linking the chapter's themes of purification and divine ease directly to the practice of Zakat.
